Date: 21/05/2026

Session: NY am

HT Bias: Wanted to see 10am open lower and look for longs as fk ass usual but we were in some annying range between the HTF rb's so i was lacking some clear bias. 

LT Bias: 10am opened higher, which was not ideal, after we sooped the ko again and created that 1m rb, it took it on the way back. Entry: 1m rb below the 10am as manipulation, after seeing it open higher and not manipulate into some sort of structure below to suport price I should not take this.

Second entry was the 3m rb of the 1h ce in the OTE of the 1H range. The 1m was a dodgy candle so iffy, 5m was weird, 3m looked nice.

Entry Time: 10:13 and 10:27

SL: both 17 points

RR: both 8 RR, midnight and 10am as targets. The problem with the second trade was super slow delivery so I started trailing, got fucked at 3.5 RR, alr I guess


Confidence: Not the highest both a 5 but im happy I atleast executed so i have something to reflect on.

Mental State during trade: Both good, no tilting just stayed calm and looked for another chance.

Mental state after trade/session: Neutral, was kinda dissapointed in the bad delivery to 10am, it also went to be and then delivered but still very slow.

Result: L-W

Lesson: Happy with the execution of trades, step in the right direction. If short bias, the 3m above. Thr key open on the OTE respecting a 1H was also valid

Woke up pretty tired, debated on not trading. Extra tired. But went on with it. I didn't believe that price would return back to that level so i switched to finding RB's. In fact i was so absorbed in the one minute time frame. definitely wasn't as sharp as i could've been. but either way, i didn't account for probabilities and while i did view that this money is out of my hands, i don't think i put it in the best situation. There was some slight nerves as the trade got tapped into, but it only lasted a few seconds as it hit my SL. There was some emotion like 'damn i lost' but no hard emotional swing like wanting to revenge trade. If price hit my initial level after and played out, then i would've been mad. But I think that should be really taken account of; "am i trading a higher probability trade over an earlier trade". The aim is always higher probability trade. So there was a bit of fomo there.

DAY 4 :  1 TRADE 1 LOSS

Technical Analysis
Bias has been longs today, though we had nvidia earnings, which made price pump and dump through asia and london session. which according to powell, makes the ny am session pretty consolidated/choppy. Originally had a limit order set at where a D OB and 15 min OB align at 29100. Saw that price was retracing from this leg to the OTE zone, price tapped a 1min OB and displace higher, i set a limit order at the wick of the low, but where my fault was was not accounting for the unmitigatedFVG right above the level. Especially that the next 1min candle wicked away from the FVG, that would have been a sign to cancel the order. There was liquidity swept, which added confluence. There should've been some patience in this trade to see how the imbalance would have played out. The same level of patience that the 10 am key open play had. I was possibly getting lost in 1min. Forgot that higher probability setups occur in the 5 minute. So if there's any learning lesson here, stick to 5 min timeframe for spotting setups. on the 5 min TF price knifed through which would have prevented me from entering on that. realistically a rejection wick forming on the 5 min would give alot more confirmation to me that a reaction is actually happening there. Always check higher time frames. Overall PA was pretty choppy so there was less probability (edited)

Pre Market: Swept PDL&asia high during london, swept london lows pre market. stacked highs above + an 1h/15m FVG. Asia low below + 1h RB. Looking for us to go to either level and see from there for a reversal or a continuation.

Choppy market open, not going anywhere.
Once we get that BoS + displacement to the upside I start looking for longs. We tap down into the gap and get a 50 pt delivery. My stop underneath the FVG candle low, tp at 50% of the higher range. We retrace fully and hit my stop for -10 pts. 

At this point I thought this was the liquidity grab for a move lower with all these strong levels to send us lower. Sweep of BSL tap into a stacked 15m and 1h FVG with a strong rejection, respect of the candle bodies, 5m RB, rebalanced. So I take the short at the rejection block and stop at the high to instantly get stopped for -20 pts.

Once we have found some exhaustion and we begin rejecting my level, the downside begins to look much cleaner. We get a 1m rejection block reaction+iFVG+BoS. On the pullback to OTE+iFVG I enter short. so usually i trade only 10 AM but i really liked that 4h RB we had once i opened the charts and we were about to go into it. we already touched it before but for me that is EL because it was way too far from the CE of the 4h RB. I wanted to see London lows getting swept (EL) and possibly touch CE and long from there with ET. NQ never reached CE but ES did and also went into the weekly gap so i already started looking for an ET on NQ because it did not look like we were gonna come down to the CE and it only missed it by 7pts which is almost mitigated on a big 4h RB lol. 

After sweeping London lows we made a nice 5m RB and i scaled downt to the 1m to find another 1m. I was ready to take the first one who touches the CE of the 5m RB but luckily the first one never got touched and the second one even mitigated .79 and presented an entry so i entered here. We also made a lot of EQH on the 1m so that another reason i was so confident in the trade. but since its not 10AM i took partials on the EQH (5 micros) and than have my final tp at the unfilled 15m gap for a 5.31 rr.

MNQ was tripping like it not only faded my tp by 3 points but also immediately wicked me to BE idk what happened there luckily i did not trail my SL. I mean i already took my partials so i dont mind what happens but if it wins im not trading 10AM and im done for the day.  but i lowkey got caught in the chop it really did look clean in the beginning. Honestly was a great trade just the time not the best because not much volume so chop could be expected. stopped me out at BE but still decent entry and delivery almost hit nicely

i put my SL a little higher because of fees but would be funny if it now delivers thats literal goy slop from NQ (edited)

Psychological Analysis
I came in to the session quite calm, i learned from the previous day to not FOMO into a trade, especially if i had a level set out. There was a moment where i saw a kaiyan strategy opening and wanted to take it, but knew that it was a form of fomo and that my level had higher probability being a 4hr fvg. part of my mind thought that it could hit the level and totally shoot up, missing my level. but i had to be confident and stick to my decision. initially i had a different level set according to rich's take but i cancelled it as soon as he did. think the takeaway here is to stick to your first decision and not change mind last minute. I was a bit bad with managing my trade, I lowered the TP cause i just wanted a win, when i should've followed the rules and let it ride to 4R if not 5R. I did account for the difference in points since SL size was 18 points. price also did move so fast that i couldn't move it in time. i thought about it for a second and it already hit. It probably was good practice to not touch it. To manage the trade well is to let price do the work. didn't get the chance to move sl to BE, but i would have. messages.author: Big_Sixty60
messages.content_text: I know what I did wrong now. My mistake wasn’t the bias or overall read — it was treating the low of the 15m rejection block as true invalidation when, realistically, during NY open on NQ that’s usually just obvious liquidity. My bullish bias still made sense from an AMT/TPO perspective because we had already swept the two single-print highs, still had four single-print lows below, absorption at VAH, and repeated failure to close below the 50% of the RB showing buyers were still defending value. Looking back, the market hadn’t fully finished seeking liquidity yet, and I entered before that process was complete. Since my stop was sitting right below the RB low — where most early longs and RB traders would naturally place stops — the market had incentive to run lower first, clear weak longs, fill larger bids, reset inventory, and then expand higher afterward. That’s why the RB “failed” but the overall thesis still played out and price hit TP later anyway. I also entered a little early because I anticipated the reversal before we got true reclaim/displacement confirming the sweep was complete. The biggest thing I took away from this is understanding the difference between actual structural invalidation and simple liquidity engineering. The higher timeframe idea wasn’t wrong — I just assumed the auction was done seeking liquidity before it actually was.

Day 4 - 20/05/26 (15m RB) (Loss)


Getting onto the chart I identified that gold was in a clear bearish trend on the HTF , and due to this I was looking to take a short entry.
,


There was not a lot of structure to see a clear idea on the 4H and 1H timeframes, but on the 15m, I saw that from 00:00, price had a steady rally up to an internal high that rebalanced into bearish FVG, followed by a strong selloff on the next candle.
,


This RB followed my criteria of sweeping liquidity, and it also contained engineered liquidity below CE before price broke out to the downside. The RB also delivered 0.62 of the current 15m bearish Price Leg.
,


Seeing this I set a LMT order at CE with my SL above the high for 3.4 points and my TP at a low that was set in off a 02:00 KO reaction back up to the RB, although I was expecting price to at least reach 00:00 as it aligned almost perfectly with 0.705 and another bullish internal 15m RB, I targeted the 02:00 level as if you are not behind a key move gold can move quite slowly.
,

Had the wrong narrative on price at the time of the trade and went into my analysis with a bearish bias I didn’t look for any reason to change. Was pretty zoomed in the lower TF’s and failed to identify that from 18:00 we had swept out PDL, and drawing the fib on the daily bearish range, an unmitigated bearish FVG CE allies perfectly with 0.5 of this daily range. An unmitigated 4H bearish FVG also aligns with 0.5 of the 4H bearish range . I am still bearish on the HTF, but I need to take more care applying High TF narrative to current LTF price. I should have also understood that the 6am 4H candle was opening in very close proximity to my 15m RB and the volatility of manipulation on a 4H candle could easily rip through such a small level in comparison.
